definition_proposal: A constricted region of a protein tunnel at which the radius available along a specified tunnel pathway reaches its minimum in a stated molecular coordinate and geometric model.
identity_discriminator: The minimum-radius region of a defined tunnel, rather than the whole passage, an enclosed disconnected void, or an experimentally demonstrated gate. A tunnel can have competing local constrictions; the minimum and its location depend on the path and conformation.

synonyms_proposal.source: Curator scope distinction: a local constriction need not be the path minimum

hierarchy_rationale: The existing TUNNEL record describes a complete passage. A bottleneck is its geometric part, not a subclass of whole tunnels. Existing CAVITY is an enclosed disconnected void, so it is not a suitable parent. Neither transport function nor selectivity is inferred.

novelty.context_adjudication: Two foundational-seeder mentions concern the existing substrate-access tunnel and its geometry. Other matches concern an allosteric network, anatomical constriction, the named Bottleneck protein, or unrelated pathway prose. None defines a separate geometric bottleneck class.
novelty.external_identifier_disposition: No authoritative one-to-one external CURIE found in the existing corpus/index or bounded web searches for tunnel bottleneck/tunnel constriction and OLS terms. The OLS exact-search API was inaccessible; this is a bounded negative finding, not an exhaustive ontology proof. No external xref is proposed. Parent owns the internal-ID prerequisite.

primary_evidence.title: CAVER 3.0: A Tool for the Analysis of Transport Pathways in Dynamic Protein Structures
primary_evidence.source_inspected: Publisher full text, definition/method section 3, Results and Figure 4, copyright notice
primary_evidence.definition_support: The method represents a pathway by maximal balls and identifies its smallest ball as the bottleneck. Neighboring residues are a separate distance-based annotation.
primary_evidence.example_support: Figure 4 and the static-versus-dynamic comparison explicitly analyze hydrogen-added 1CQW, 1BN6 and 1BN7 models. The p1 bottleneck radius calculated for 1CQW is 1.3 angstrom. That is a model-dependent computed radius, not an experimental measurement or universal threshold.
primary_evidence.source_license: CC-BY; publisher notice names Creative Commons Attribution License without a version in the inspected text
primary_evidence.license_notice_locator: Publisher article copyright paragraph following publication dates
primary_evidence.redistribution_disposition: Compatible attribution terms verified. Use original factual synthesis with attribution; no article prose, figures, tables, or coordinates copied. Do not relabel the source article CC-BY-4.0 merely because the project synthesis uses that license.

method.name: CAVER 3.0 command-line pathway bottleneck geometry
method.documentation_inspected: Native CAVER user guide, pages 5-9, 21-23, 32, 40-41, 48-49 and 72; downloaded and text-extracted on 2026-10-28
method.version_scope: Documented CAVER 3.0 command-line package; the guide also documents version 3.01 corrections. Record the exact executable build/checksum for execution. Neither installed nor executed in this audit.
method.software_and_manual_license: GPL-3.0, explicitly stated at beginning of native guide; software/manual retain this license and are not relabeled as project data
method.input: A directory of PDB structures; multiple structures must be aligned with consistent atom/residue numbering. Preserve input file names and a fixed seed for reproducibility. CAVER home must contain bin and lib resources. Java 6 or higher is the documented requirement, not a guarantee for every later runtime.
method.required_config: At least one of starting_point_coordinates x y z, starting_point_atom <serials>, or starting_point_residue <chain:residue identifiers>. The start has no default and must be justified for the target tunnel. Select included atoms, hydrogen/protonation treatment, ligands and waters explicitly.
method.config_notes: The final three values are documented reporting defaults/settings, not class thresholds. Tune probe/shell/clustering settings to the molecular system and retain them. The 3-angstrom residue contact distance annotates neighbors of the bottleneck; it does not define the bottleneck radius.
method.output: {output}/analysis/bottlenecks.csv: per-snapshot tunnel/cluster identity, bottleneck center X/Y/Z, radius, and nearby residues. Check against tunnel profiles and retain all tied/alternative minima when relevant.
method.decision_rule: For a source-selected, structurally valid tunnel path, localize the smallest unobstructed ball along its axis. This is the bottleneck candidate under the stated model. Confirm path identity and connectivity; the tool does not infer physiological transport or gating from geometry.
limitations: Static coordinates do not establish conformational persistence, access kinetics, ligand passage, or gating function.
Atomic radii, hydrogen treatment, missing atoms, assembly, starting point, path search, probe and shell settings affect the result.
Profile sampling and numerical approximation affect bottleneck localization. The guide documents version-dependent geometric changes.
Clustering can merge/split path identities; default per-snapshot tunnel selection can discard alternatives.
No universal positive radius cutoff defines this class; it is relative to the specified tunnel. A flat or tied minimum needs explicit reporting.

representative.evidence_source: DOI:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002708; Figure 4 and static crystal-structure pathway analysis
representative.role: Whole-structure representative of a source-computed tunnel bottleneck; not a qualified canonical protein example
representative.state: NaI-cocrystallized haloalkane dehalogenase; the CAVER paper analyzed a hydrogen-added model
representative.source_rights: PDB archive data CC0-1.0 per https://www.wwpdb.org/about/usage-policies; this does not relicense the crystallography article
representative.qualification_status: NOT_QUALIFIED; no source-asserted UniProt coordinates or release receipt

record_license_proposal: CC-BY-4.0 for project-authored factual synthesis and annotations only; cited CAVER article CC-BY, software/manual GPL-3.0, PDB data CC0-1.0 retain source-specific terms
causal_graph_disposition: Do not fabricate a universal causal graph. This card establishes a geometric part and a computational representative, not a class-wide transport or catalysis mechanism.
